_comment: WHERE AN ACTOR'S FEET ARE, AND HOW ITS ANIMATIONS ARE TIMED -- authored,
not guessed. Before this file the runtime inferred all three of those
numbers by scanning pixels and applying global constants, and every
inference was eventually wrong about something: the golem's ground slam
erupts an earth spike ~50px BELOW its feet and Shawn's idle plants a staff
~33px below his, so a scan for 'the lowest opaque pixel' read both as the
floor and hoisted the figures off the ground. See docs/ART_PIPELINE.md.
groundLine: pixels from the sprite canvas's BOTTOM EDGE up to the surface
the figure stands on. One value per actor, not per stance, because a
character's feet do not move relative to their own art -- only the effects
drawn around them do. That is what stops a figure jumping between poses.
breath: how hard this creature breathes, as a multiplier on the transform
breath every idle figure now carries (see Domain/Stage/BreathCurve). It is
the one number here that is a JUDGEMENT rather than a measurement, so it is
also the one with a rule behind it: unset means 1.0 for an actor whose idle
is a single drawing and 0.35 for one whose sheet already moves. Author it
only where that rule is wrong about a particular sheet. Negative means none.
stances: only poses with MORE THAN ONE FRAME need an entry, since timing
is meaningless for a still. StanceManifestValidationTests fails if a
multi-frame stance is missing one, so this cannot silently fall behind the
art. Single-frame poses take the defaults in StanceManifestResolver.
Lives in Resources/ rather than ContentData/ because it is read at RUNTIME
rather than baked by ContentBuilder, and deliberately NOT under
Resources/Content/, which ContentBuilder deletes wholesale on every run.

actors._groundLineNote: Dropped from 12 to 8 when the flat single-drawing idle was replaced by a 12-frame idle sheet -- re-slicing the whole actor together moves every stance onto one shared canvas, and 8 is what that canvas measures. Re-confirmed 2026-08-30 against the regenerated 3x4 idle sheet: still 8, now with all 29 poses agreeing within 1px (was 2px).

stances._paceNote: Doubled from 0.08 (2026-08-30) -- reported as breathing much too fast. 0.08 was inherited from the 6-frame sheet this stance used to have, where it meant 0.48s per half-breath; the 12-frame sheet kept the per-FRAME number and so ran the same motion in the same time with twice the frames, which is not the same animation. At 0.16 a half-breath is 1.92s and the full ping-pong cycle 3.84s, the slowest idle on the roster -- correct for a creature that is standing still and waiting. Compare beetle 6x0.20 (2.40s full) and treant 6x0.14 (1.68s full).

stances._impactFrameNote: Re-measured (2026-08-30) against the CURRENTLY delivered 12-frame sheet -- the previous note here (impactFrame 7, f6) was already stale, measured against an earlier version of this same sheet before it was re-sliced; the numbers it quoted (519px, next-highest 504px) do not match what is on disk now. Fresh measurement: f5 (0-indexed, so frame 6 here) has the furthest bbox right edge of all 12 delivered frames (608px, next-highest f6 at 570px), and is also visibly the peak of the leap by eye -- fully airborne, mouth widest, claws at full extension -- with f6 already showing the front paws landing. Re-measure again if this sheet is re-sliced; a note that says a specific pixel value is only true of one specific file on disk, not of 'the attack sheet' in general.

actors._breathNote: Higher than the 0.35 a six-frame idle defaults to, because this sheet barely moves. Measured across its own delivered idle, aligned as the stage aligns it: the head travels 7px on a 470px figure, against the Treant's 22px on 425px. The default assumes a sheet that already breathes is doing a third of the work; this one is doing closer to a tenth, and the churn it does have (13% of the silhouette per step) is redrawing rather than motion. See BreathCurve.
actors._groundLineNote: Every forest_warden frame was cropped independently to its own content bounding box plus a uniform 14px pad on every side, rather than sliced off one shared-canvas sheet the way golem/rat were -- so this value is that pad, not a measured foot position. It should hold well for idle/attack/attack_roar/attack_charge, where the feet are consistently each frame's lowest point; hurt and defeated change body orientation enough that a small vertical pop between stances is possible and worth an eyeball pass in the editor.

stances._note: 0.2 rather than the 0.1 every other Warden stance runs at, on request -- the roar reads as the fight's turning point and was over faster than its plain swing. Doubling the pace doubles the beat: FightBeatPlayer budgets a beat at secondsPerFrame x FrameCount, so nothing in code had to change for this.

actors._deliveryNote: Delivered via docs/STANCE_SHEET_SPEC.md's Stage 1/Stage 2 process -- one ChatGPT-generated animation sheet per stance, sliced by tools/slice_actor_sheet.py. Supersedes the earlier undocumented pad_actor_frames.py delivery. groundLine measured from the sliced idle sheet. The idle is a half-breath, ping-pong by default (see Domain/Stage/LoopCycle) -- not a complete cycle, so no loop override.

stances._idleNote: Slower than the delivered 0.14 (it read as breathing too fast) with a half-second hold on the full-inhale peak -- endHold is dead time at the top of the ping-pong so the breath pauses there rather than lingering equally at both ends. See LoopCycle.FrameAt.

stances._returnsNote: Shell Up curls into the sealed ball (frames 1-6) then uncurls back to neutral (6-1) rather than snapping from the ball to idle. The uncurl is the curl played backwards -- no extra art. See StanceStepper.PlayReverse.

actors._groundLineNote: As above. The slam lands when the trunk is fully over (f3) and the spore burst when the arms reach their widest (f4).
